title: Avalanche Size and Interevent Time Statistics in Amorphous System
authors: Thomas Muhren, Roberto Benzi, Mauro Sbragaglia, Jeannot Trampert, Federico Toschi
abstract: The intermittent, stick-slip flow of amorphous systems is characterized by avalanches whose statistical properties display robust power-laws. In this paper, we study avalanche statistics in a field theoretical model of a soft-glassy system under shear. The order parameter in our model is the fluidity, which is related to the local rate of plastic events in a soft-glass. While avalanche sizes $S$ have been extensively characterized, the statistics of interevent times $t_i$ have remained largely unexplored. Here, we find that both $S$ and $t_i$ are power-law distributed and that their scaling exponents satisfy a precise relation. The model enables the analytical derivation of the scaling exponents and the reproduction of the behavior observed across a wide class of amorphous systems.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the statistical mechanics of avalanches in amorphous materials using a field-theoretic model. It determines that both avalanche sizes and interevent times exhibit power-law scaling, and crucially, it derives a precise mathematical relationship connecting their respective scaling exponents. The work provides analytical predictions that successfully match numerical simulations of soft-glassy systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the statistical properties of avalanches (size $S$ and interevent time $t_i$) in amorphous systems, with a specific focus on characterizing the interevent time statistics.
main_result: Both avalanche sizes and interevent times are found to follow power-law distributions, and their respective scaling exponents satisfy a precise theoretical relationship ($\gamma = 3 - 2\alpha$).
method: The study employs a field theoretical model of a soft-glassy system under shear, deriving scaling laws by analyzing the evolution of the fluidity order parameter $\phi$ and its associated probability distributions.
model_or_system: The system is a soft-glassy amorphous material modeled by coupled, nonlinear partial differential equations describing stress ($\Sigma$) and fluidity ($\phi$). The analysis utilizes simplified, space-independent versions of these equations.
key_observables: Avalanche size distribution $P[S] \sim S^{-5/4+\delta/2}$ and interevent time distribution $P[t_i]$, along with the correlation coefficient $r$ between $S$ and $t_i$.
important_parameters: The scaling exponent $\delta$ is a crucial parameter controlling the exponents for both $S$ and $t_i$; the critical value $\delta = 1/2$ is highlighted.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on significant simplifications, including assuming constant stress rate ($\dot{\Gamma} = 0.01$) and using approximations like the Self-Consistent Field Approximation (Hartree method) to solve the dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the stress evolution showing stress drops (avalanches), the joint probability density of $t_i$ and $S$, and the collapse of the conditional interevent time distribution $P[t_i|\lambda S_0]$ onto a Gamma distribution.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the full dynamical model (stress and fluidity) to simplifying it into solvable forms. It then derives the power-law scaling for $P[S]$ and $P[t_i]$ separately, establishes the relationship between their exponents, and discusses the implications of the critical parameter $\delta$.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical derivation of scaling relations between two distinct statistical measures ($S$ and $t_i$) in a non-equilibrium, disordered system provides a powerful theoretical framework applicable to many complex physical processes.
